rule: Elixir: `defimpl P, for: T` members -> `P.T.fun` | `defimpl P, for: [A, B]` members are `P.A.f` and `P.B.f` (one edge per type). | Body-less member declarations of scanned types are defined in the scan (high): a call that resolves to a method declared without a body by a trait, interface, protocol ... is high when that declaring type is in the scan
notes: call_type convention (SPEC gives no Elixir mapping; Elixir has no methods and the `macro` type is defined only for C/C++/ObjC and Rust `name!`): every local, imported and remote call is direct, a call through a value is callback. Operators and special forms (`|>`, `=`, `case`, `fn`, `%{}`, `__MODULE__`) are language constructs, not calls. P = MyApp.Shape, T = MyApp.Circle gives `MyApp.Shape.MyApp.Circle.*` (Elixir's own impl module name). The list form gives one edge per type for each call in the shared body (lines 7, 8). `MyApp.Shape.area` is the body-less protocol declaration in shape.ex: in the scan, so high, and listed in nodes (C1). `c.r` / `s.dims` are field access. `&MyApp.Shape.area/1` is a capture, not a call. `def area(shape)` in defprotocol is a declaration.
